'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russo-Ukrainian War]]
**[[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***[[Russian Armed Forces|Russian forces]] strike [[Kyiv]]'s energy system facilities and launch [[BM-30 Smerch]] missiles on [[Zaporizhzhia]] as [[Ukraine]] repels attacks in the [[Donbas]]. [https://www.rferl.org/a/ukraine-russia-strikes-kyiv-zaporizhzhia-crazy-tactics/32102668.html (RFE/RL)]
*[[Syrian civil war]]
**[[Iran–Israel conflict during the Syrian civil war]]
***[[Israel]] carries out [[airstrike]]s near [[Damascus]], [[Syria]], killing four pro-[[Iran]]ian fighters. [https://english.alarabiya.net/News/middle-east/2022/10/27/Four-pro-Iranian-fighters-killed-in-Israeli-strikes-near-Damascus-War-monitor (Al Arabiya)]
*[[2022 Haitian crisis]], [[Canada–Haiti relations]]
**[[Canada]] sends a delegation to [[Haiti]] to assess the security situation and to "consult with stakeholders on options to support Haitian people in resolving the humanitarian and security crises", amid ongoing international talks on sending a [[peacekeeping]] force to the country. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2022/10/27/canada-sends-delegation-to-haiti-to-assess-security-crisis (Al Jazeera)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[Decommunization]]
**[[Poland|Polish]] authorities demolish four [[Polish People's Republic|communist-era]] monuments to the [[Red Army]] in the respective towns of [[Głubczyce]], [[Byczyna]], [[Bobolice]], and [[Staszów]], citing a 2016 law that prohibits promotion of [[totalitarianism|totalitarian]] regimes. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/av/world-europe-63414842 (BBC News)] [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2022/10/27/poland-removes-four-communist-era-red-army-monuments (Al Jazeera)] 

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Acquisition of Twitter by Elon Musk]]
**Entrepreneur [[Elon Musk]] acquires [[Twitter, Inc.]] in a [[$]]44bn deal. Musk fires [[Twitter]]'s chief executive officer [[Parag Agrawal]], chief financial officer Ned Segal, and the head of legal policy [[Vijaya Gadde]] upon taking over. [https://www.ft.com/content/b429b624-bf82-4ccd-bf69-b75055403952 (''Financial Times'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*A [[firefighting aircraft]] of the Italian [[Protezione Civile]] crashes on [[Mount Etna]] in [[Sicily]] while fighting a forest fire, killing the two pilots on board. [https://www.emergency-live.com/news/tragedy-in-sicily-canadair-crashes-to-the-ground-two-pilots-on-board-die/amp/ (''Emergency-live.com'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[Israeli–Lebanese maritime border dispute]]
**The [[Israeli cabinet]] unanimously votes in favor of approving a [[United States|US]]-brokered maritime deal with [[Lebanon]], with [[Prime Minister of Israel|Prime Minister]] [[Yair Lapid]] hailing the deal as an "enemy state's formal recognition". [https://www.timesofisrael.com/israel-approves-lebanon-deal-lapid-hails-recognition-by-enemy-state/ (''Times of Israel'')]
*[[China–Netherlands relations]]
**The [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Netherlands)|Ministry of Foreign Affairs]] of the [[Netherlands]] announces an investigation regarding the activities of [[China]]'s two allegedly illegal police stations in the country. [https://edition.cnn.com/2022/10/27/europe/netherlands-china-illegal-police-stations-intl/index.html (CNN)]
'''Law and crime'''
*[[LGBT rights in Russia]]
**The [[State Duma]] unanimously gives preliminary approval to a bill strengthening a law against "[[Russian gay propaganda law|propaganda of non-traditional sexual relations]]". The bill will expand the ban on "propaganda" to all ages, and will outlaw media and online resources, including films, books, and theater productions. [https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/russian-lawmakers-vet-bill-lgbtq-propaganda-92182570 (ABC News)]
*[[Crime in Italy]]
**One person is killed and five others, including Spanish [[association football|footballer]] [[Pablo Marí]], are injured during a [[mass stabbing]] at a [[Carrefour]] supermarket in [[Assago]], [[Lombardy]], [[Italy]]. The perpetrator, a man with mental health problems, who used a knife from a shelf, is arrested at the scene. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-63421228 (BBC News)]
*Eight people, all members of one family, are found dead in and around a house in [[Broken Arrow, Oklahoma|Broken Arrow]], [[Oklahoma]], United States. The incident is being investigated as a possible [[murder-suicide]]. [https://apnews.com/article/fires-homicide-tulsa-oklahoma-a873c9e0cd6e52968a1ff912d23f6af2 (AP)]
